question: Do differences in family life-history composition predict how differently two families allocate phylogenetic memory among traits?
population: AusTraits matched positive-numeric log core; 42 families, 254 systems, 13 traits.

rank_disagreement.definition: fraction of non-tied shared trait-pair comparisons whose relative order differs between the two families

predictors.woody_distance: absolute difference in family woody_fraction where both families have woody_fraction
predictors.combined_strategy_distance: Euclidean distance in standardized perennial_fraction and woody_fraction where both are available

association.statistic: Spearman correlation between predictor distance and rank disagreement
association.null: 9999 permutations of complete family predictor profiles among family identities, preserving the fixed observed rank-disagreement graph

hard_nonclaims: Australian-flora family composition is not assumed to equal global family composition.
A null result does not exclude finer ecological drivers.
Do not interpret pairwise non-independence with naive parametric p values; use the family-label permutation.
